prerequisites: An honest account of what caused the shortfall
A specific, credible recovery plan and timeline
steps: State plainly, on one slide, that the mistake was made and own it without spinning it.
Explain in plain terms exactly what happened and what led to the hole.
Lay out the specific plan to get out of it.
Give a recovery timeline and payback window the other side can price.
State the specific amount needed and exactly what is offered in return.
Keep it to five slides; the goal is a credible plan, not a full data room.

test.method: Track response rate and terms offered when this deck is used versus a longer or less structured pitch.
test.measure: Response rate, terms secured, time to close the ask
test.read_point: After each use of the deck

title: Screen a founder's character with mutual reference calls before a deal
hypothesis: If both sides of an acquisition run reference calls on each other's past partners before closing, then a deal with someone hard to work with gets caught before signing, because the source argues a great deal cannot survive a bad person on the other side of it.
does_not_apply_when: A deal with no ongoing working relationship after close, where character fit matters less than terms alone.

signal.check: An acquisition, partnership or takeover is being evaluated mainly on terms and numbers, with no character check run in either direction.

expected_effect.size: unknown, source states this as its own strong filter, not a measured result

risk.note: A reference-call step only; it can surface a reason to walk away before any commitment is made.

prerequisites: Contact details for past partners or counterparties of the person on the other side of the deal
steps: Before closing, ask the other side for reference calls with their past partners or counterparties.
Offer the same on your own side, so the check runs both ways.
Ask direct questions about how the person behaves under pressure and whether the referee would work with them again.
Treat a clear character red flag as a reason to walk away, even on otherwise strong terms.
When forced to choose between a strong asset with a weak counterpart and a weaker asset with a strong one, weigh the counterpart heavily.

test.method: Track deal outcomes for acquisitions or partnerships that ran this check against ones that did not.
test.measure: Post-close dispute rate, deal_failure_rate
test.read_point: 12 months after each deal closes

title: Evaluate an internal capability as a picks-and-shovels product for other brands
hypothesis: If a capability built for the store's own use, such as packaging sourcing, cross-border logistics or a procurement system, is tested as a paid service for other brands, then a proven internal advantage can turn into its own revenue line, because the same cost-saving the store already gets can be sold to a brand that has not built it.
does_not_apply_when: A capability that is still a working advantage over competitors and would lose value if shared with other brands.

signal.check: The store has a sourcing, logistics or procurement capability that peers and mentees repeatedly ask about or overpay for elsewhere, and it has never been tested as its own offer.

expected_effect.size: unknown, source's own pipeline figure is interest generated by content, not booked revenue

risk.note: Productizing an internal tool too early can pull attention from the core store while it still creates more value staying internal.

prerequisites: A capability that is genuinely proven internally, not just planned
A way to validate demand from peers before investing further
steps: List internal capabilities that solve a problem other brands are known to struggle with.
Validate real demand by talking to peers or mentees before building anything new.
Design the offer so the value to the other brand is concrete, such as a clear cost saving.
Test the offer with one or two outside brands before treating it as a real product line.
Use content or direct outreach to generate interest and track it as a pipeline, not as booked revenue until it closes.

test.method: Run a small pilot of the capability as a paid service with 1 to 2 outside brands before any further investment.
test.measure: Pilot conversion rate, outside-brand cost saving delivered, hours diverted from the core store
test.read_point: After the pilot period with the first outside brands
